newsitem.title: POLAND: PRESIDENT SETS POLISH ELECTION FOR SEPTEMBER 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESIDENT SETS POLISH ELECTION FOR SEPTEMBER 14.

text.p: President Aleksander Kwasniewski has set the date of Poland's parliamentary elections for September 14, a source close to the president said on Wednesday.
"The president will announce the September 14 date of the elections during his televised address to the nation tonight," the source, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
By law, the elections have to held on a day free of work within a month before the end of parliament's term, which falls for October 14 this year.
The polls, the third free parliamentary elections since the fall of communism in 1989, will pit the ruling ex-communists against a rightist opposition bloc gathered around the Solidarity trade union.

With opinion polls showing both ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the opposition Solidarity Election Action (AWS) supported by about 25 percent, the balance of power in the next parliament could be held by smaller parties.

Both groups adhere to pro-market policies and integration with the European Union and NATO. The Solidarity's platform is oriented to religious and patriotic values while the SLD, in power since 1993 along with the Peasant Party (PSL), is pragmatic and secular.
